prompt.query: Determine the bond dissociation energy of the sodium dimer Na2 (a single-sigma-bond metal dimer). Species SMILES: [Na][Na]; target SMILES: [Na].[Na]; total charge 0, multiplicity 1; conditions: gas phase. Atom-mapped reactant SMILES: [Na:1][Na:2]. The 1-based map numbers in it are the indexing convention for `bond_changes` (keep using the plain SMILES above for graph nodes and evidence annotations). Model the process you investigate as a graph and maintain `mechanism_graph.json` in the sandbox root: nodes for every species or electronic state you characterize (with SMILES) and edges for the state changes or transformations between them (with `via` pointing to the TS node id when a transition state was located). Extra nodes or edges beyond the reference are never penalized, so record every state you actually characterized. Every elementary-step edge must carry `bond_changes`: `break`/`form` lists of [i, j] atom-map index pairs, where [i, j] belongs to `break` if the bond order between atoms i and j decreases over the step (including full cleavage) and to `form` if it increases (including newly formed bonds); a purely conformational or state-change step carries two empty lists. Every computational evidence file you produce for a species or step (QM input or log) must carry a `smiles: <SMILES>` comment line identifying the species, so the scorer can bind each graph element to concrete evidence. The scorer reads this file forensically; a missing or unparseable file severely impacts the score. In your final summary you must report the Na2 bond dissociation energy in kcal/mol and its equilibrium bond length in Angstrom. If you conclude that the requested quantity cannot be computed to a trustworthy accuracy with the allowed methods, you must say so explicitly in your final summary and explain the electronic-structure reason; do not report a number you cannot stand behind. Run the computations with ORCA or Gaussian: the scorer parses only these two programs' log formats, so output from any other program cannot count as evidence. Allowed computational methods are limited to MACE-OMol25 and xTB; calls beyond the whitelist are intercepted.

edges.step_type: Na-Na bond stretching to the separated-atom dissociation limit
